newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end week softer in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end week softer in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwe stocks closed active but weaker with brokers predicting share prices -- which they said had become too expensive during recent bull run -- were likely to continue falling in a correction next week.
"Today we saw a lot of sellers in heavy volumes on the market and this should continue next week," one broker said.
"I think we might see a 10 percent drop (in the main industrial index) within less than a month before we see buyers coming in again," the broker said.
On Friday, the 57-share industrial index shed 30.17 points to close at 10,291.51 although it closed 459.98 points up on the week.

The day's losers included bankers Barclays, 200 cents down at 3,600, retail and hotel giant Meikles which lost 50 cents to 2,050, and finance group Finhold which eased by 25 cents to 875, while building firm Mashonaland Holdings and tea and coffee grower EHPL both lost 15 cents to 250 and 155.

However, a number of gains were recorded, namely in banking group FMB which added 400 cents to 6,100, tobacco firm Rothmans which put on 200 to 6,500 and clothing retailer Edgars and food and winemaker Cairns which went up 100 cents to 5,100 and 1,550 respectively, while Radar put on 50 cents to 650.

Also traded firmer were wine producers Afdis, 30 cents stronger at 530 while publishing group Zimpapers at 2,800, sugar growers Hippo at 1425 and Zimbabwe Sugar Refineries at 1,500 all gained 25 cents. Wire and Cable company Bicaf added 20 cents to 400.

Minings were mixed in thin trading with Alloys Mines, 20 cents up at 140, the only winner of the day. Coal giant Wankie lost 25 cents to 575 and Falgold eased five cents to 95, pushing the seven-share index 2.83 points lower to 1,116.30. This was a 38.27 fall on the week. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 27/8/9--
